paragraphs.text: Now concerning the things whereof ye wrote: It is good for a man not to touch a woman.
paragraphs.original: Περὶ δὲ ὧν ἐγράψατε, καλὸν ἀνθρώπῳ γυναικὸς μὴ ἅπτεσθαι·
paragraphs.translit: Peri de hōn egrapsate, kalon anthrōpō gynaikos mē haptesthai·

paragraphs.text: But, because of fornications, let each man have his own wife, and let each woman have her own husband.
paragraphs.original: διὰ δὲ τὰς πορνείας ἕκαστος τὴν ἑαυτοῦ γυναῖκα ἐχέτω, καὶ ἑκάστη τὸν ἴδιον ἄνδρα ἐχέτω.
paragraphs.translit: dia de tas porneias hekastos tēn heautou gynaika echetō, kai hekastē ton idion andra echetō.

paragraphs.text: Let the husband render unto the wife her due: and likewise also the wife unto the husband.
paragraphs.original: τῇ γυναικὶ ὁ ἀνὴρ τὴν ὀφειλὴν ἀποδιδότω, ὁμοίως δὲ καὶ ἡ γυνὴ τῷ ἀνδρί.
paragraphs.translit: tē gynaiki ho anēr tēn opheilēn apodidotō, homoiōs de kai hē gynē tō andri.

paragraphs.text: The wife hath not power over her own body, but the husband: and likewise also the husband hath not power over his own body, but the wife.
paragraphs.original: ἡ γυνὴ τοῦ ἰδίου σώματος οὐκ ἐξουσιάζει ἀλλὰ ὁ ἀνήρ· ὁμοίως δὲ καὶ ὁ ἀνὴρ τοῦ ἰδίου σώματος οὐκ ἐξουσιάζει ἀλλὰ ἡ γυνή.
paragraphs.translit: hē gynē tou idiou sōmatos ouk exousiazei alla ho anēr· homoiōs de kai ho anēr tou idiou sōmatos ouk exousiazei alla hē gynē.

paragraphs.text: Defraud ye not one the other, except it be by consent for a season, that ye may give yourselves unto prayer, and may be together again, that Satan tempt you not because of your incontinency.
paragraphs.original: μὴ ἀποστερεῖτε ἀλλήλους, εἰ μήτι ἂν ἐκ συμφώνου πρὸς καιρὸν ἵνα σχολάσητε τῇ προσευχῇ καὶ πάλιν ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ ἦτε, ἵνα μὴ πειράζῃ ὑμᾶς ὁ Σατανᾶς διὰ τὴν ἀκρασίαν ὑμῶν.
paragraphs.translit: mē apostereite allēlous, ei mēti an ek symphōnou pros kairon hina scholasēte tē proseuchē kai palin epi to auto ēte, hina mē peirazē hymas ho Satanas dia tēn akrasian hymōn.

paragraphs.text: But this I say by way of concession, not of commandment.
paragraphs.original: τοῦτο δὲ λέγω κατὰ συγγνώμην, οὐ κατʼ ἐπιταγήν.
paragraphs.translit: touto de legō kata syngnōmēn, ou katʼ epitagēn.

paragraphs.text: Yet I would that all men were even as I myself. Howbeit each man hath his own gift from God, one after this manner, and another after that.
paragraphs.original: θέλω δὲ πάντας ἀνθρώπους εἶναι ὡς καὶ ἐμαυτόν· ἀλλὰ ἕκαστος ἴδιον ἔχει χάρισμα ἐκ θεοῦ, ὁ μὲν οὕτως, ὁ δὲ οὕτως.
paragraphs.translit: thelō de pantas anthrōpous einai hōs kai emauton· alla hekastos idion echei charisma ek theou, ho men houtōs, ho de houtōs.

paragraphs.text: But I say to the unmarried and to widows, It is good for them if they abide even as I.
paragraphs.original: Λέγω δὲ τοῖς ἀγάμοις καὶ ταῖς χήραις, καλὸν αὐτοῖς ἐὰν μείνωσιν ὡς κἀγώ·
paragraphs.translit: Legō de tois agamois kai tais chērais, kalon autois ean meinōsin hōs kagō·

paragraphs.text: But if they have not continency, let them marry: for it is better to marry than to burn.
paragraphs.original: εἰ δὲ οὐκ ἐγκρατεύονται, γαμησάτωσαν, κρεῖττον γάρ ἐστιν γαμῆσαι ἢ πυροῦσθαι.
paragraphs.translit: ei de ouk enkrateuontai, gamēsatōsan, kreitton gar estin gamēsai ē pyrousthai.

paragraphs.text: But unto the married I give charge, [yea] not I, but the Lord, That the wife depart not from her husband
paragraphs.original: Τοῖς δὲ γεγαμηκόσιν παραγγέλλω, οὐκ ἐγὼ ἀλλὰ ὁ κύριος, γυναῖκα ἀπὸ ἀνδρὸς μὴ χωρισθῆναι—
paragraphs.translit: Tois de gegamēkosin parangellō, ouk egō alla ho kyrios, gynaika apo andros mē chōristhēnai—

paragraphs.text: (but should she depart, let her remain unmarried, or else be reconciled to her husband); and that the husband leave not his wife.
paragraphs.original: ἐὰν δὲ καὶ χωρισθῇ, μενέτω ἄγαμος ἢ τῷ ἀνδρὶ καταλλαγήτω— καὶ ἄνδρα γυναῖκα μὴ ἀφιέναι.
paragraphs.translit: ean de kai chōristhē, menetō agamos ē tō andri katallagētō— kai andra gynaika mē aphienai.

paragraphs.text: But to the rest say I, not the Lord: If any brother hath an unbelieving wife, and she is content to dwell with him, let him not leave her.
paragraphs.original: Τοῖς δὲ λοιποῖς λέγω ἐγώ, οὐχ ὁ κύριος· εἴ τις ἀδελφὸς γυναῖκα ἔχει ἄπιστον, καὶ αὕτη συνευδοκεῖ οἰκεῖν μετʼ αὐτοῦ, μὴ ἀφιέτω αὐτήν·
paragraphs.translit: Tois de loipois legō egō, ouch ho kyrios· ei tis adelphos gynaika echei apiston, kai hautē syneudokei oikein metʼ autou, mē aphietō autēn·

paragraphs.text: And the woman that hath an unbelieving husband, and he is content to dwell with her, let her not leave her husband.
paragraphs.original: καὶ γυνὴ εἴ τις ἔχει ἄνδρα ἄπιστον, καὶ οὗτος συνευδοκεῖ οἰκεῖν μετʼ αὐτῆς, μὴ ἀφιέτω τὸν ἄνδρα.
paragraphs.translit: kai gynē ei tis echei andra apiston, kai houtos syneudokei oikein metʼ autēs, mē aphietō ton andra.

paragraphs.text: For the unbelieving husband is sanctified in the wife, and the unbelieving wife is sanctified in the brother: else were your children unclean; but now are they holy.
paragraphs.original: ἡγίασται γὰρ ὁ ἀνὴρ ὁ ἄπιστος ἐν τῇ γυναικί, καὶ ἡγίασται ἡ γυνὴ ἡ ἄπιστος ἐν τῷ ἀδελφῷ· ἐπεὶ ἄρα τὰ τέκνα ὑμῶν ἀκάθαρτά ἐστιν, νῦν δὲ ἅγιά ἐστιν.
paragraphs.translit: hēgiastai gar ho anēr ho apistos en tē gynaiki, kai hēgiastai hē gynē hē apistos en tō adelphō· epei ara ta tekna hymōn akatharta estin, nyn de hagia estin.

paragraphs.text: Yet if the unbelieving departeth, let him depart: the brother or the sister is not under bondage in such [cases]: but God hath called us in peace.
paragraphs.original: εἰ δὲ ὁ ἄπιστος χωρίζεται, χωριζέσθω· οὐ δεδούλωται ὁ ἀδελφὸς ἢ ἡ ἀδελφὴ ἐν τοῖς τοιούτοις, ἐν δὲ εἰρήνῃ κέκληκεν ἡμᾶς ὁ θεός.
paragraphs.translit: ei de ho apistos chōrizetai, chōrizesthō· ou dedoulōtai ho adelphos ē hē adelphē en tois toioutois, en de eirēnē keklēken hēmas ho theos.

paragraphs.text: For how knowest thou, O wife, whether thou shalt save thy husband? Or how knowest thou, O husband, whether thou shalt save thy wife?
paragraphs.original: τί γὰρ οἶδας, γύναι, εἰ τὸν ἄνδρα σώσεις; ἢ τί οἶδας, ἄνερ, εἰ τὴν γυναῖκα σώσεις;
paragraphs.translit: ti gar oidas, gynai, ei ton andra sōseis; ē ti oidas, aner, ei tēn gynaika sōseis;

paragraphs.text: Only, as the Lord hath distributed to each man, as God hath called each, so let him walk. And so ordain I in all the churches.
paragraphs.original: Εἰ μὴ ἑκάστῳ ὡς ἐμέρισεν ὁ κύριος, ἕκαστον ὡς κέκληκεν ὁ θεός, οὕτως περιπατείτω· καὶ οὕτως ἐν ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις πάσαις διατάσσομαι.
paragraphs.translit: Ei mē hekastō hōs emerisen ho kyrios, hekaston hōs keklēken ho theos, houtōs peripateitō· kai houtōs en tais ekklēsiais pasais diatassomai.

paragraphs.text: Was any man called being circumcised? Let him not become uncircumcised. Hath any been called in uncircumcision? Let him not be circumcised.
paragraphs.original: περιτετμημένος τις ἐκλήθη; μὴ ἐπισπάσθω· ἐν ἀκροβυστίᾳ κέκληταί τις; μὴ περιτεμνέσθω.
paragraphs.translit: peritetmēmenos tis eklēthē; mē epispasthō· en akrobystia keklētai tis; mē peritemnesthō.

paragraphs.text: Circumcision is nothing, and uncircumcision is nothing; but the keeping of the commandments of God.
paragraphs.original: ἡ περιτομὴ οὐδέν ἐστιν, καὶ ἡ ἀκροβυστία οὐδέν ἐστιν, ἀλλὰ τήρησις ἐντολῶν θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: hē peritomē ouden estin, kai hē akrobystia ouden estin, alla tērēsis entolōn theou.

paragraphs.text: Let each man abide in that calling wherein he was called.
paragraphs.original: ἕκαστος ἐν τῇ κλήσει ᾗ ἐκλήθη ἐν ταύτῃ μενέτω.
paragraphs.translit: hekastos en tē klēsei hē eklēthē en tautē menetō.

paragraphs.text: Wast thou called being a bondservant? Care not for it: nay, even if thou canst become free, use [it] rather.
paragraphs.original: Δοῦλος ἐκλήθης; μή σοι μελέτω· ἀλλʼ εἰ καὶ δύνασαι ἐλεύθερος γενέσθαι, μᾶλλον χρῆσαι.
paragraphs.translit: Doulos eklēthēs; mē soi meletō· allʼ ei kai dynasai eleutheros genesthai, mallon chrēsai.

paragraphs.text: For he that was called in the Lord being a bondservant, is the Lord`s freedman: likewise he that was called being free, is Christ`s bondservant.
paragraphs.original: ὁ γὰρ ἐν κυρίῳ κληθεὶς δοῦλος ἀπελεύθερος κυρίου ἐστίν· ὁμοίως ὁ ἐλεύθερος κληθεὶς δοῦλός ἐστιν Χριστοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: ho gar en kyriō klētheis doulos apeleutheros kyriou estin· homoiōs ho eleutheros klētheis doulos estin Christou.

paragraphs.text: Ye were bought with a price; become not bondservants of men.
paragraphs.original: τιμῆς ἠγοράσθητε· μὴ γίνεσθε δοῦλοι ἀνθρώπων.
paragraphs.translit: timēs ēgorasthēte· mē ginesthe douloi anthrōpōn.

paragraphs.text: Brethren, let each man, wherein he was called, therein abide with God.
paragraphs.original: ἕκαστος ἐν ᾧ ἐκλήθη, ἀδελφοί, ἐν τούτῳ μενέτω παρὰ θεῷ.
paragraphs.translit: hekastos en hō eklēthē, adelphoi, en toutō menetō para theō.

paragraphs.text: Now concerning virgins I have no commandment of the Lord: but I give my judgment, as one that hath obtained mercy of the Lord to be trustworthy.
paragraphs.original: Περὶ δὲ τῶν παρθένων ἐπιταγὴν κυρίου οὐκ ἔχω, γνώμην δὲ δίδωμι ὡς ἠλεημένος ὑπὸ κυρίου πιστὸς εἶναι.
paragraphs.translit: Peri de tōn parthenōn epitagēn kyriou ouk echō, gnōmēn de didōmi hōs ēleēmenos hypo kyriou pistos einai.

paragraphs.text: I think therefore that this is good by reason of the distress that is upon us, [namely,] that it is good for a man to be as he is.
paragraphs.original: νομίζω οὖν τοῦτο καλὸν ὑπάρχειν διὰ τὴν ἐνεστῶσαν ἀνάγκην, ὅτι καλὸν ἀνθρώπῳ τὸ οὕτως εἶναι.
paragraphs.translit: nomizō oun touto kalon hyparchein dia tēn enestōsan anankēn, hoti kalon anthrōpō to houtōs einai.

paragraphs.text: Art thou bound unto a wife? Seek not to be loosed. Art thou loosed from a wife? Seek not a wife.
paragraphs.original: δέδεσαι γυναικί; μὴ ζήτει λύσιν· λέλυσαι ἀπὸ γυναικός; μὴ ζήτει γυναῖκα·
paragraphs.translit: dedesai gynaiki; mē zētei lysin· lelysai apo gynaikos; mē zētei gynaika·

paragraphs.text: But shouldest thou marry, thou hast not sinned; and if a virgin marry, she hath not sinned. Yet such shall have tribulation in the flesh: and I would spare you.
paragraphs.original: ἐὰν δὲ καὶ γαμήσῃς, οὐχ ἥμαρτες. καὶ ἐὰν γήμῃ ἡ παρθένος, οὐχ ἥμαρτεν. θλῖψιν δὲ τῇ σαρκὶ ἕξουσιν οἱ τοιοῦτοι, ἐγὼ δὲ ὑμῶν φείδομαι.
paragraphs.translit: ean de kai gamēsēs, ouch hēmartes. kai ean gēmē hē parthenos, ouch hēmarten. thlipsin de tē sarki hexousin hoi toioutoi, egō de hymōn pheidomai.

paragraphs.text: But this I say, brethren, the time is shortened, that henceforth both those that have wives may be as though they had none;
paragraphs.original: τοῦτο δέ φημι, ἀδελφοί, ὁ καιρὸς συνεσταλμένος ἐστίν· τὸ λοιπὸν ἵνα καὶ οἱ ἔχοντες γυναῖκας ὡς μὴ ἔχοντες ὦσιν,
paragraphs.translit: touto de phēmi, adelphoi, ho kairos synestalmenos estin· to loipon hina kai hoi echontes gynaikas hōs mē echontes ōsin,

paragraphs.text: and those that weep, as though they wept not; and those that rejoice, as though they rejoiced not; and those that buy, as though they possessed not;
paragraphs.original: καὶ οἱ κλαίοντες ὡς μὴ κλαίοντες, καὶ οἱ χαίροντες ὡς μὴ χαίροντες, καὶ οἱ ἀγοράζοντες ὡς μὴ κατέχοντες,
paragraphs.translit: kai hoi klaiontes hōs mē klaiontes, kai hoi chairontes hōs mē chairontes, kai hoi agorazontes hōs mē katechontes,

paragraphs.text: and those that use the world, as not using it to the full: for the fashion of this world passeth away.
paragraphs.original: καὶ οἱ χρώμενοι τὸν κόσμον ὡς μὴ καταχρώμενοι· παράγει γὰρ τὸ σχῆμα τοῦ κόσμου τούτου.
paragraphs.translit: kai hoi chrōmenoi ton kosmon hōs mē katachrōmenoi· paragei gar to schēma tou kosmou toutou.

paragraphs.text: But I would have you to be free from cares. He that is unmarried is careful for the things of the Lord, how he may please the Lord:
paragraphs.original: Θέλω δὲ ὑμᾶς ἀμερίμνους εἶναι. ὁ ἄγαμος μεριμνᾷ τὰ τοῦ κυρίου, πῶς ἀρέσῃ τῷ κυρίῳ·
paragraphs.translit: Thelō de hymas amerimnous einai. ho agamos merimna ta tou kyriou, pōs aresē tō kyriō·

paragraphs.text: but he that is married is careful for the things of the world, how he may please his wife,
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ γαμήσας μεριμνᾷ τὰ τοῦ κόσμου, πῶς ἀρέσῃ τῇ γυναικί,
paragraphs.translit: ho de gamēsas merimna ta tou kosmou, pōs aresē tē gynaiki,

paragraphs.text: and is divided. [So] also the woman that is unmarried and the virgin is careful for the things of the Lord, that she may be holy both in body and in spirit: but she that is married is careful for the things of the world, how she may please her husband.
paragraphs.original: καὶ μεμέρισται. καὶ ἡ γυνὴ ἡ ἄγαμος καὶ ἡ παρθένος μεριμνᾷ τὰ τοῦ κυρίου, ἵνα ᾖ ἁγία καὶ τῷ σώματι καὶ τῷ πνεύματι· ἡ δὲ γαμήσασα μεριμνᾷ τὰ τοῦ κόσμου, πῶς ἀρέσῃ τῷ ἀνδρί.
paragraphs.translit: kai memeristai. kai hē gynē hē agamos kai hē parthenos merimna ta tou kyriou, hina ē hagia kai tō sōmati kai tō pneumati· hē de gamēsasa merimna ta tou kosmou, pōs aresē tō andri.

paragraphs.text: And this I say for your own profit; not that I may cast a snare upon you, but for that which is seemly, and that ye may attend upon the Lord without distraction.
paragraphs.original: τοῦτο δὲ πρὸς τὸ ὑμῶν αὐτῶν σύμφορον λέγω, οὐχ ἵνα βρόχον ὑμῖν ἐπιβάλω, ἀλλὰ πρὸς τὸ εὔσχημον καὶ εὐπάρεδρον τῷ κυρίῳ ἀπερισπάστως.
paragraphs.translit: touto de pros to hymōn autōn symphoron legō, ouch hina brochon hymin epibalō, alla pros to euschēmon kai euparedron tō kyriō aperispastōs.

paragraphs.text: But if any man thinketh that he behaveth himself unseemly toward his virgin [daughter], if she be past the flower of her age, and if need so requireth, let him do what he will; he sinneth not; let them marry.
paragraphs.original: Εἰ δέ τις ἀσχημονεῖν ἐπὶ τὴν παρθένον αὐτοῦ νομίζει ἐὰν ᾖ ὑπέρακμος, καὶ οὕτως ὀφείλει γίνεσθαι, ὃ θέλει ποιείτω· οὐχ ἁμαρτάνει· γαμείτωσαν.
paragraphs.translit: Ei de tis aschēmonein epi tēn parthenon autou nomizei ean ē hyperakmos, kai houtōs opheilei ginesthai, ho thelei poieitō· ouch hamartanei· gameitōsan.

paragraphs.text: But he that standeth stedfast in his heart, having no necessity, but hath power as touching in his own heart, to keep his own virgin [daughter], shall do well.
paragraphs.original: ὃς δὲ ἕστηκεν ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ ἑδραῖος μὴ ἔχων ἀνάγκην, ἐξουσίαν δὲ ἔχει περὶ τοῦ ἰδίου θελήματος, καὶ τοῦτο κέκρικεν ἐν τῇ ἰδίᾳ καρδίᾳ, τηρεῖν τὴν ἑαυτοῦ παρθένον, καλῶς ποιήσει·
paragraphs.translit: hos de hestēken en tē kardia autou hedraios mē echōn anankēn, exousian de echei peri tou idiou thelēmatos, kai touto kekriken en tē idia kardia, tērein tēn heautou parthenon, kalōs poiēsei·

paragraphs.text: So then both he that giveth his own virgin [daughter] in marriage doeth well; and he that giveth her not in marriage shall do better.
paragraphs.original: ὥστε καὶ ὁ γαμίζων τὴν παρθένον ἑαυτοῦ καλῶς ποιεῖ, καὶ ὁ μὴ γαμίζων κρεῖσσον ποιήσει.
paragraphs.translit: hōste kai ho gamizōn tēn parthenon heautou kalōs poiei, kai ho mē gamizōn kreisson poiēsei.

paragraphs.text: A wife is bound for so long time as her husband liveth; but if the husband be dead, she is free to be married to whom she will; only in the Lord.
paragraphs.original: Γυνὴ δέδεται ἐφʼ ὅσον χρόνον ζῇ ὁ ἀνὴρ αὐτῆς· ἐὰν δὲ κοιμηθῇ ὁ ἀνήρ, ἐλευθέρα ἐστὶν ᾧ θέλει γαμηθῆναι, μόνον ἐν κυρίῳ·
paragraphs.translit: Gynē dedetai ephʼ hoson chronon zē ho anēr autēs· ean de koimēthē ho anēr, eleuthera estin hō thelei gamēthēnai, monon en kyriō·

paragraphs.text: But she is happier if she abide as she is, after my judgment: and I think that I also have the Spirit of God.
paragraphs.original: μακαριωτέρα δέ ἐστιν ἐὰν οὕτως μείνῃ, κατὰ τὴν ἐμὴν γνώμην, δοκῶ δὲ κἀγὼ πνεῦμα θεοῦ ἔχειν.
paragraphs.translit: makariōtera de estin ean houtōs meinē, kata tēn emēn gnōmēn, dokō de kagō pneuma theou echein.
